title: Fibre products of formal algebraic spaces are formal algebraic spaces
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for formal algebraic spaces X and Y over a sheaf Z whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, the fibre product of X and Y over Z is a formal algebraic space (statement lines 3487-3493). The proof first chooses presentations of the two spaces and observes that the induced family of fibre products is a family of representable etale morphisms onto the fibre product, so that by locality of the definition it suffices to treat the case where both spaces are affine (proof lines 3495-3505). In that case both spaces are written as filtered colimits of affine schemes, the fibre product is rewritten as the colimit of the fibre products of the stages, each of which is an algebraic space, and the transition morphisms between these fibre products are shown to be thickenings because they are compositions of base changes of thickenings (proof lines 3507-3518). The conclusion follows from the statement that a filtered colimit of algebraic spaces glued by thickenings is a formal algebraic space (proof lines 3514-3518). The claim is H2: the reduction to the affine case is a locality argument with a covering whose members are representable and etale, and the affine case requires writing the colimit and verifying the thickening property of the transition maps.
